title: Highness Microelectronics Ltd - 544741 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14.5% to INR16.11 crore and PAT rose 66.9% to INR4.10 crore, with management guiding FY27 revenue of INR30-32 crore.
summary.overview: Highness Microelectronics reported FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) as its strongest year since listing on BSE SME: revenue INR16.11 crore (+14.5% YoY), EBITDA INR6.61 crore (+46%), and PAT INR4.10 crore (+66.9%). Management attributed margin gains to favourable project mix and high-margin contracts, and said H2 has historically been stronger than H1. Growth plans centre on a Goa facility for COG/FOG display manufacturing, a glass cutting line at Rabale, and an MoU with Axiom (USA). Management did not give a clean H2 standalone revenue figure, and several answers on order book and margins were loosely quantified.

financial_highlights.change: +46% YoY (vs INR4.51 crore); margin ~46% vs ~33% in FY25 per CFO
+66.9% YoY (vs INR2.45 crore); PAT margin 25% vs 17.5%
vs negative INR1.425 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash used in investing activities

segments.name: Defense and aerospace
segments.commentary: Largest segment at ~39% of revenue (~INR6.38 crore). Includes avionics-grade rugged backlights; management cited ~INR6.3 crore from aerospace in response to an analyst question.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: ~21.1% of revenue (~INR4.36 crore). Contracted orders with 6-18 month firm forecasts; stretched bar displays for metro and coach passenger information.

segments.name: Medical and healthcare
segments.commentary: ~26.7% of revenue (~INR4.30 crore). Orders come through OEM partners and a pan-India dealer network in staggered fashion.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: revenue INR30-32 crore, EBITDA margin ~35%, PAT above 25%.
FY28 target: revenue above INR50 crore with similar margins (EBITDA ~35%, PAT ~25%) plus potential uplift from new lines.
Steady-state target once Goa lines mature: EBITDA ~30-32% and PAT 15-17%.
Confirmed projections of INR30 crore over the next 18 months; unexecuted POs of INR8-10 crore (later cited as INR8.5-9 crore) to be executed in the current quarter.
Long-term ambition: revenue near INR300 crore in about four years, though CEO said it could come sooner than five years.
capex_capacity: Glass cutting line at Rabale (Navi Mumbai): machines already ordered; expected operational by end-July, latest mid-August 2026. Targets railway and metro stretched displays.

Goa electronic manufacturing cluster: land acquired; paperwork underway; construction to start after approvals; first commercial production about a year from now (around July-August 2027) for COG/FOG.
Goa capex in phases: phase 1 machines INR10-12 crore, phase 2 INR8-10 crore; total ~INR20 crore excluding civil work.
Management said automation would lift capacity utilisation from the current ~20% level; processes are largely manual today.
Backward integration: COG/FOG lines to replace imported open-cell glass (from China/Taiwan), with expected input cost reduction of 8-10% once the line is set up and ~15% at maturity.
demand_pricing: Display glass is sourced from Far East Asia; value addition is done at Rabale. Value addition in defence/surveillance is ~40-50% of product cost, which management expects to rise above 50% (towards 60%) with new machines.
Railway and metro orders are contracted with firm 6-18 month forecasts; defence and aerospace uses design wins plus display volume projections; medical is OEM and dealer driven.
Lead times: railways ~8 weeks, medical 4-5 weeks, avionics and defence 12-14 weeks.
Three design wins with an Australian customer (railway and aerospace) have generated an estimated INR5-6 crore of revenue; three more railway designs are expected to close in FY27.
Export receivable of about INR2.5 crore delayed; one tranche came in January, another expected in June, and full collection is expected by end-September 2026.
Management says the unofficial Indian market for imported railway/metro displays is several thousand crore; it targets 10% share, then 20%, then 50%. Current share is below 1%.

Automotive-grade displays: certification takes about a year after the Goa facility is up; management targets entry around two years out, starting with two-wheeler and commercial vehicle makers (Mahindra has shown interest).

qa_highlights.question: How much Chinese component reliance is there, and are CKD/SKD units being assembled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it supplies imaging solutions (TFT LCD displays and support electronics) to system integrators. Basic glass comes from Far East Asia and is ruggedised and value-added at Rabale to meet defence specs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 gross and EBITDA margins jump, and are they sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 EBITDA margin was ~46% (vs ~33%) on favourable project mix and high-margin contracts. He expects margins to stay healthy but warned of quarterly fluctuation from project timing and mix.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for Goa and when does first commercial production start?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 machines INR10-12 crore and phase 2 INR8-10 crore, about INR20 crore total excluding civil work. First commercial production is about a year away (around July-August 2027).

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of orders: one-time or contractual?
qa_highlights.answer: Railway orders are contractual with 6-18 month firm forecasts. Medical is partner and dealer driven with staggered orders. Defence has design wins plus display volume projections.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capex needed when capacity utilisation is around 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Goa plant is for backward integration to stop importing open-cell glass. Automation of manual processes at existing facilities is expected to lift utilisation sharply.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 guidance of INR30-32 crore achievable given flat historic revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is achievable because the company is recruiting a sales team and applying for central and state subsidies. Management did not give a bridge from the current order book.

risks_watch: Revenue execution: confirmed projections of INR30 crore over 18 months and unexecuted POs of only INR8.5-9 crore imply heavy reliance on new orders to hit FY27 guidance.
Margin normalisation: FY26 EBITDA margin of ~46% was driven by export and high-margin projects; management guides a steady state of ~30-35%.
Goa execution timelines (construction, approvals, machine induction) and the Rabale glass-cutting line due by July-August 2026.
Working capital: INR2.5 crore export receivable delayed and expected to clear only by end-September 2026.
Concentration and geopolitics: dependence on Far East Asia glass supply; freight costs up on fuel surcharge due to Middle East disruption.
Certification timelines for automotive-grade displays (about 2 years) and for new defence and railway design wins.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term targets (FY28 revenue above INR50 crore, three-digit revenue ambition), but vague or hedged on near-term specifics: the CEO said he did not have an exact figure for design-win revenue, and the CFO gave loose order book and margin numbers. Notably, the call repeated numerous forward figures without giving a bridge.
key_quotes: So we get basic displays, basic glass from Far East Asia and then we ruggedize it, we value add some features to those displays so that it qualifies for the defense requirements and we supply it to the system integrators.
This COG, FOG facility is basically a backward integration process.
Once everything settles and business is mature as you are saying, our EBITDA margin should be around 30%, 32% in normal case and 15% to 17% as PAT.

adds.what: Glass cutting line at Rabale (Navi Mumbai), machines already ordered
Goa electronic manufacturing cluster for COG/FOG display lines (phase 1 machines INR10-12 crore, phase 2 INR8-10 crore; ~INR20 crore total excl. civil work)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR30-32 crore (~30% midpoint growth on FY26's INR16.11 crore), backed partly by INR8.5-9 crore of unexecuted POs and a Rabale glass cutting line due end-July/mid-August 2026, but the Goa COG/FOG capacity (first production ~July-August 2027) comes later and the call gave no clean H2 standalone figure.
